About

Sourcing that holds up when the program cannot slip.

I lead Joby Aviation's Electronics Global Supply Chain team, owning more than $100M in annual spend across the electronics that power a next generation eVTOL aircraft and its charging infrastructure.

My range is the difference. I move from semiconductor shortage strategy to should cost teardown to executive negotiation, and make each legible to leadership so the right call gets made fast.

Across 7+ years I have built supply chains from zero, qualified Tier 1 EMS partners, recovered line downs in weeks, and de risked tens of millions in exposure. Recognized with the SPX Silver Star Award and promoted three times along the way.

Leadership, for me, is influence and ownership, not headcount. I align design, program, quality, and executives to land decisions, translate complex supply and cost risk into decision ready narratives up to CEO and CFO level, and mentor GSMs and SIEs, whether I manage the team or sit beside it.

Should cost and contracts

The two levers a GSM lives on.

Leverage starts with knowing the true cost of a part and holding it in the contract. Here is the approach, worked through on a SiC power module.

SiC power module, bottoms up should costRaw material to finished module
Materials69%
SiC MOSFET and diode die45%
Ceramic substrate, AMB or DBC10%
Copper or AlSiC baseplate4%
Silver sinter die attach3%
Bond wires and ribbons2%
Power terminals and leadframe2%
Housing, silicone gel, and consumables3%
Conversion and process14%
Die attach and sintering3%
Wire and ribbon bonding3%
Substrate, baseplate, and terminal assembly3%
Encapsulation and cure1%
Final test and reliability screen3%
Yield loss1%
Burden and commercial17%
Equipment depreciation and factory overhead6%
SG&A4%
Packaging, logistics, and duties2%
Supplier margin5%
Estimated finished module cost100%
Illustrative of the approach, not actual pricing. The percentages show a bottoms up structure for a SiC power module, built up from raw material through conversion to a finished module, so the gap to any supplier quote becomes visible and negotiable.
LIVE MARKET DATA

Agentic AI should cost model

A dynamic model I built with AI agents. It pulls live market data such as SiC wafer, copper, silver, and energy prices, computes the bottoms up cost from raw material to finished module, and keeps the gap to a supplier quote updating as inputs move.

Yes, in the ways that matter most. I have not run an AI datacenter program by that name, but I have sourced its building blocks and built real infrastructure that maps directly onto it.

  • Infrastructure I have built. Stood up the supply chain and buildout for autonomous robot fulfillment centers, launching two across Texas and New Jersey. That is hardware and site infrastructure from the ground up.
  • Commodity breadth. Deep across electronics, electrical, mechanical, and plastics, from silicon, memory, and power modules to PCBAs, harnesses, and machined and molded parts. Datacenter hardware lives in exactly these commodities.
  • Adjacency at scale. I qualify and hold Tier 1 contract manufacturers accountable, run should cost and cost management, and de risk constrained silicon, the same disciplines compute infrastructure demands.
  • Proven ramp. I have built supply chains from zero more than once, so a new domain is a fast on ramp, not a gamble.

So this is not a from scratch learning curve. It is a strong, directly relevant foundation with a short, focused ramp on the datacenter specifics.
